5	-/
6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartUnivReduce
8	
9	/-!
10	# The coupling of the atlas open to the coverage witness
11	
12	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` (`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) has three antecedents, and
13	the board tracks them on three separate rows: `IsChartUniv` (c9b), Zariski-local surjectivity
14	of `Sigma.desc f` (dat-b B-6), and `rep i` (divrep).  Reading those rows one concludes the
15	three compose — discharge each and the seam fires.
16	
17	**They do not compose as stated.**  The atlas the seam consumes is a family of *restricted*
18	charts `restrictChart (abelSigmaChart …) (V i)` (`Picard/Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree.lean:86`),
19	whose source is `(V i : Scheme)` — an open of the *chart source*, i.e. of the divisor scheme.
20	So the coverage antecedent, unfolded through `chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise`
21	(`Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean:128`), must produce a chart point
22	`x : (W : Scheme) ⟶ (V i : Scheme)` landing **in that same `V i`**, while coverage geometry
23	produces a point of the divisor scheme `D.left` with no such constraint.  The two opens the
24	route wants to identify live on different objects — `V i` on the divisor scheme, `chartLocus`
25	on the test — and no declaration in the tree relates them.
26	
27	That is an obligation *between* two antecedents, owned by no row, and it is why "close c9b,
28	then close B-6" would not have composed even with both closed.
29	
30	## What this file does about it
31	
32	It names the coupling and derives restricted coverage from unrestricted coverage together
33	with a range containment: the coverage witness, viewed in the chart source, factors
34	set-theoretically through `V i`.  Given that, the witness lifts to `V i` along the open
35	immersion `(V i).ι` by `IsOpenImmersion.lift`, and the class it names is unchanged because
36	`restrictChart` is *by definition* precomposition with `yoneda.map (V i).ι` — so the lift's
37	chart value is the unlifted one, with no transport.
38	
39	**THREE CORRECTIONS TO AN EARLIER DRAFT OF THIS HEADER**, all from a fresh-context audit
40	(2026-07-29, inbox `I-0894`), because each would have mispriced the row:
41	
42	1. the hypothesis is **NOT "weaker than either antecedent"**, as the draft claimed.  It is the
43	   unrestricted coverage datum **conjoined** with the containment, so it *implies* the
44	   coverage antecedent and is strictly STRONGER than it.  What is true is the much smaller
45	   claim that the containment is all that separates unrestricted from restricted coverage;
46	2. `liftPointwiseToOpens` and `pointwise_of_pointwise_restrictChart` together are one
47	   **biconditional**, and its transport step (`restrictChart_app_apply`) is `rfl`.  So this
48	   file is a *repackaging with its difference named*, and **it closes no gate**.  It is
49	   reported as routing information, not as progress on any antecedent;
50	3. the draft argued about "`V i = chartLocus`" in two places.  **Those carriers do not meet**:
51	   `V i : (X i).Opens` is an open of the chart source (the divisor scheme), while
52	   `chartLocus C m Z lam : Set ↥T.left` is a set on a *test*.  The only bridge is
53	   `chartLocusOpens`, which lands in `T.left.Opens` and costs `haff` (= dat-b's B-4).  The
54	   mismatch is precisely what this file was written to expose, so reasoning as though the two
55	   were interchangeable — as the draft did below — defeated the purpose.
56	
57	What survives all three: the containment is genuine content (probes below), it is exactly the
58	difference between the two coverage statements (the converse), and no declaration in the tree
59	relates the two carriers.
60	
61	## Main declarations
62	
63	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PointwiseCoverage` — the pointwise coverage datum of B-5, named for an
64	  arbitrary chart family so the two atlases (unrestricted, restricted) can be compared.
65	* `AlgebraicGeometry.liftPointwiseToOpens` — **the coupling**: pointwise coverage for a family
66	  `f` plus the range containment gives pointwise coverage for the *restricted* family
67	  `fun i => restrictChart (f i) (V i)`.
68	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_restrictChart_of_pointwise` — the composite into the
69	  instance the seam consumes, for the restricted atlas.
70	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pointwise_of_pointwise_restrictChart` — the **converse**: restricted
71	  coverage gives unrestricted coverage *and* the containment.  So `hV` is not a hypothesis
72	  chosen for provability — it is exactly the difference between the two, and a lane cannot
73	  reach the restricted atlas while avoiding it.
74	-/
75	
76	set_option autoImplicit false
77	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
78	
79	universe u
80	
81	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
82	
83	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
84	
85	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
86	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
87	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
88	
89	noncomputable section
90	
91	variable (C) in
92	/-- **The pointwise coverage datum of B-5**, named.
93	
94	This is verbatim the hypothesis of `chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise`
95	(`Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean:128`), given a name so that the same statement can be
96	compared at two different chart families — which is the whole point of this file: B-6 is
97	consumed at the *restricted* atlas, while coverage geometry produces the datum at the
98	*unrestricted* one. -/
99	def PointwiseCoverage {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
100	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) : Prop :=
101	  ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
102	    ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
103	      (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s
104	
105	/-! ## The chart value of a restricted chart at a lifted point -/
106	
107	/-- **A restricted chart reads a lifted point exactly as the unrestricted chart reads the
108	point itself.**
109	
110	`restrictChart f V` is `yoneda.map V.ι ≫ f` by definition, so its value at `u` is the value
111	of `f` at `u ≫ V.ι`.  No transport, no naturality of `f` — the composition is on the source
112	side, where `yoneda.map` is precomposition.
113	
114	This is the entire reason the coupling below is cheap, and it is worth isolating: a lane that
115	expected the two chart values to differ by a restriction map would look for a compatibility
116	that is not needed. -/
117	lemma restrictChart_app_apply {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
118	    (V : X.Opens) {S : Scheme.{u}} (u : S ⟶ (V : Scheme.{u})) :
119	    (restrictChart f V).app (op S) u = f.app (op S) (u ≫ V.ι) :=
120	  rfl
121	
122	/-! ## The coupling -/
123	
124	variable (C) in
125	/-- **THE COUPLING**: pointwise coverage for `f` plus a range containment gives pointwise
126	coverage for the restricted family.
127	
128	The containment is the honest content: at the point, index and witness coverage produces, the
129	witness's image in the chart source lies inside `V i`.  Everything else is the lift along the
130	open immersion `(V i).ι` and `restrictChart_app_apply`, which is `rfl` — so this direction
131	carries no mathematics beyond the lift, and together with its converse below it is a
132	biconditional rather than a reduction.  **It closes no gate.**
133	
134	Note the shape of the hypothesis: it quantifies over the data coverage *returns*, not over all
135	opens or all witnesses.  So a producer discharges it exactly where it produces the witness,
136	which is the only place the information is available; a formulation asking for the containment
137	uniformly over all witnesses would be strictly stronger.
138	
139	What the containment *means* geometrically depends on which open `V i` is, and this file
140	deliberately does not assume an answer — in particular `V i` is an open of the chart source
141	while `chartLocus` is a set on a test, so the two are not interchangeable and the intended
142	instantiation still owes the `chartLocusOpens` bridge (cost: `haff`, i.e. dat-b's B-4). -/
143	theorem liftPointwiseToOpens {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
144	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (V : ∀ i, (X i).Opens)
145	    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
146	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
147	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s ∧
148	          Set.range (x.base) ⊆ Set.range ((V i).ι.base)) :
149	    PointwiseCoverage C (fun i => restrictChart (f i) (V i)) := by
150	  intro T s t
151	  obtain ⟨W, htW, i, x, hx, hrange⟩ := h T s t
152	  refine ⟨W, htW, i, IsOpenImmersion.lift ((V i).ι) x hrange, ?_⟩
153	  rw [restrictChart_app_apply, IsOpenImmersion.lift_fac]
154	  exact hx
155	
156	variable (C) in
157	/-- **The composite**: coverage plus the containment gives the local-surjectivity instance
158	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes *at the restricted atlas* — which is the atlas
159	`mixedParamRepresentableBy` (`Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree.lean:125`) and every real chart family
160	is built from.
161	
162	Stated because this, not `isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise`, is what a coverage lane
163	owes when the atlas is restricted: the two differ by exactly `hV`. -/
164	theorem isLocallySurjective_restrictChart_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
165	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (V : ∀ i, (X i).Opens)
166	    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
167	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
168	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s ∧
169	          Set.range (x.base) ⊆ Set.range ((V i).ι.base)) :
170	    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
171	      (Sigma.desc (fun i => restrictChart (f i) (V i))) :=
172	  isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise C _ (liftPointwiseToOpens C f V h)
173	
174	/-! ## The converse: `hV` is the exact difference, not a convenient extra
175	
176	A coupling lemma whose hypothesis is stronger than the gap it bridges hides the gap instead of
177	naming it.  This section rules that out: restricted coverage gives back unrestricted coverage
178	together with the containment, so `hV` is precisely what separates the two. -/
179	
180	variable (C) in
181	/-- **The converse of the coupling.**  Pointwise coverage for the restricted family gives
182	pointwise coverage for `f` *and* the range containment at the produced witness.
183	
184	So `liftPointwiseToOpens`' hypothesis is not a strengthening chosen to make the proof go: it
185	is logically equivalent to the conclusion.  In particular a lane cannot obtain B-6 for the
186	restricted atlas — the one the seam consumes — while avoiding the statement that coverage hits
187	its classes inside `V i`.
188	
189	The witness is `x ≫ (V i).ι`, whose range is contained in that of `(V i).ι` by construction,
190	and whose chart value under `f i` is the restricted chart's value at `x` by

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivSchemeFrameCover

/-!
# The ε-identity does not consume a certificate: it consumes the WINDOW QUOTIENT

`Picard/DivRepChartClassUnivAny.lean` weakened U2's residue from "the `Classical.choose`n
adaptation is certified" to "*some* adaptation is certified"
(`ThetaGeneratorSeed.HasCertifiedAdaptation`).  A fresh-context review then observed that the
weakened form is **refuted** by `forall_not_isCertified_of_straddling`
(`Picard/DivisorFamilyAffStrict.lean`) whenever the seed's local equations are connected and
meet both pinned vertical fibres — that theorem concludes `∀ A n, ¬ A.IsCertified n`, so it
refutes an existential over adaptations exactly as it refutes a property of one adaptation.
The `…divrep.u2` row was left **unpriced**.

**This file re-prices it, and the answer is that the refutation misses the target.**  Unfold
what the ε-identity actually consumes:

* `divFamEps` is two `divisorWindow`s (`Picard/DivisorFamilyWindow.lean`), and
  `divisorWindow d` reads **only** `d` — no cover, no adaptation, no chart typing;
* `divisorWindow_eq_of_le` (`Picard/DivSchemeEps.lean`) is the rank engine
  `Submodule.eq_of_le_of_rankAtStalk_quotient_eq` applied to the pair
  `x.toSubmodule ≤ divisorWindow d`.  That engine's hypotheses are three module-theoretic
  facts about the **window quotient** `(R ⊗[k] H_a) ⧸ K_a(d)`.

The adaptation appears in the landed statement only as a *vehicle* for those three facts:
`windowQuotEquiv` transports them from `A.ThetaGlued a`, and `IsCertified` is what makes
`A.ThetaGlued a` finite projective of rank `g`.  Cut the vehicle out and the hypothesis is

> `(R ⊗[k] H_a) ⧸ K_a(d)` is projective over `R` of constant fibre rank `g`.

**Finiteness is not among the inputs, and that is measured rather than assumed.**  The rank
engine takes its `Module.Finite` slot at the *Grassmannian point's* quotient, which
`grFunctorAff` carries as a field; so the window side owes only projectivity and the rank
equation.  The landed chart-typed statement threads finiteness of `A.ThetaGlued a` as well —
that hypothesis is genuinely unused on the window side, and dropping it is what the
`unusedVariables` linter reported when this file first elaborated.

**Why this matters, and it is the point of the file.**  That statement mentions no
adaptation, so `forall_not_isCertified_of_straddling` does not bear on it: the no-go's proof
runs through clause **(c1)** of `IsCertified` (finiteness of the *chart-local colength*
modules forces `supportLeak = ∅`, hence confinement to one pinned chart —
`supportLocus_subset_chart_of_isCertified`).  A statement about the window quotient of `d`
is not an instance of the refuted `∀`.  So the ε-half of U2 is **open, not false**, and the
no-go's bite is confined to the *class* half.

## The honest partition this file establishes

U2 asks a producer for two things at the universal point, and only one of them is what the
no-go refutes:

| half | what it needs | vs. the no-go |
|---|---|---|
| the **ε-value** | `d`'s window quotient is projective of rank `g` | untouched: no adaptation |
| the **class** | a term of `DivFamZar C R_Z π g` (locally certified) | the refuted half |

So the `…divrep.u2` row should be read as: the ε-layer is carrier-free and no-go-immune, and
the whole remaining bite of `I-0705` is on producing the class — which is precisely the half
protection `I-0492`'s widening (R2) exists to supply.  That is a strictly sharper statement
than "unpriced", and it is what tells the certificate lane which face to widen.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.divisorWindow_eq_of_le_of_quotientData` — the ε-projection identity's
  window form from the window quotient alone: no `DivisorAdaptation`, no `IsCertified`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.divisorWindow_eq_of_le_of_isCertified_of_quotientData` — the landed
  chart-typed statement recovered as a corollary, so the generalisation is machine-checked
  rather than asserted.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.divFamEps_eq_of_le_of_quotientData` — the ε-**pair** identity for an
  arbitrary `F : DivFam C R π g`, from window-quotient data at the two pinned windows.  This
  is the form a widened producer can feed, and it never mentions a carrier.

## What this does NOT do

It produces no certificate, no adaptation and no class, so **no gate clears**: nothing here
lets a consumer instantiate `DivRepAffinePullback`.  It re-partitions the debt and removes a
*refutation* from one half of it.  Critical-path §7.6 (L8) is untouched.

**The honest limit of the headline, and it is the probe this file does not run.**  "The ε-half is
open, not false" is a claim about the **no-go**: `forall_not_isCertified_of_straddling` does not
bear on a hypothesis that names no adaptation.  It is *silent about satisfiability*.  The mirror
risk is real and unmeasured: if the window quotient at the universal point can never be
projective of constant rank `g`, then this file has reduced U2's ε-half to a **false**
hypothesis — and such a reduction passes every `sorry` census and every axiom probe, because it
is then a theorem.

Note the asymmetry with the junk-witness probe that refuted DAT-J's Abel square
(`Picard/JacobianDataAbelSquareVacuity.lean`): *that* residue was vacuous because its witness was
**consumer-chosen**.  Here the window quotient is determined by `d`, so vacuity is impossible and
satisfiability is the only live failure mode.  A reduction owes both checks; this one carries
"not silently stronger" (the corollary above, which recovers the landed statement) and owes the
satisfiability one.
-/

/-!
# U2's scalar side condition is a genus disjunction, not an obligation

`Picard/DivRepChartClassUniv.lean` reduced the DDR9-U ε-identity at the universal point
to two inputs: a certificate `IsCertified g` at the high-window universal seed, and the
scalar `hb : 0 < windowBound π hπ`.  The roadmap leaf `…divrep.u2` then recorded `hb` as
a *side condition to be discharged*, with the warning that `windowBound` is a
`Classical.choose` from a predicate upward-closed in `b`, so "some valid bound is
positive" is trivial while "the chosen one is" is not.

**The warning was right about the shape and wrong about the state.**  The tree already
carries the discharge, and has since the F3 ledger extension:

> `genus_eq_zero_of_windowBound_nonpos` (`RiemannRoch/WindowLedgerF3.lean`) —
> `windowBound ≤ 0` makes `windowBound_spec` fire at the **zero** divisor, so
> `h¹(𝒪) = 0`, and with the normalizations `h⁰(𝒪) = 1`, `χ(𝒪) = 1 − g` that forces
> `g = 0`.

So `hb` is not an obligation: it is a genus disjunction whose degenerate branch is
already proved.  `WindowLedgerF3` itself uses exactly this pattern twice
(`two_mul_genus_le_S_mul_windowδ`, `two_mul_genus_le_M_mul_windowδ`) — every consumer
`by_cases`es on `windowBound ≤ 0` and lands in `g = 0`.

This file draws that consequence for U2's own inputs, at the ledger data U2 uses:
`hO`, `hχ` over `C.left` are exactly `genus_eq_zero_of_windowBound_nonpos`'s
normalizations at `Y = C.left`, `K = k`.  So **`hb` follows from `g ≠ 0`**, and the
ε-identity at the universal point needs no scalar hypothesis once `g ≠ 0` — which every
consumer of a genus-`g` Jacobian has, `g = 0` being the case where `Pic⁰` is trivial.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.windowBound_pos_of_genus_ne_zero` — `g ≠ 0 → 0 < windowBound π hπ`,
  from the ledger normalizations alone.  General: no seed, no chart, no universal point.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.PointwiseAchiever.divFamEps_highWindow_eq_universal_pair_of_ne_zero`
  — the U2 ε-identity with `hb` replaced by `g ≠ 0`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.PointwiseAchiever` ·
  `exists_certifiedFamily_divFamEps_eq_universal_pair_of_ne_zero` and `divFamZarUnivOfNeZero`
  — the existential and the `DivFamZar` class, same swap.

## What this does NOT do

It produces no certificate.  U2's residue after this file is **exactly one statement**,
`IsCertified g` at the high-window universal seed's adaptation over the chart ring — no
scalar beside it.  L8 (critical-path §7.6) is untouched and remains the campaign's real
gate.
-/

78	For every test `T` and every degree-zero class `s` on it, the maps into `T` along which `s`

84	index.  It never has to mention `Sigma.desc` or the coproduct of yoneda presheaves.  Turning
85	that into the coproduct form is `isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc` below. -/
86	def ChartsCoverLocally {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
87	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) : Prop :=
88	  ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)),

92	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes.
93	
94	The proof is the bookkeeping the row's name hides: the image sieve of `Sigma.desc f` contains
95	the image sieve of every individual `f i` — because a `T'`-point of `X i` gives a `T'`-point
96	of the coproduct through `Sigma.ι` — hence contains their supremum, and a sieve containing a
97	covering sieve is covering.

100	imposes no coherence condition across indices (the observation `Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree.lean`

102	exactly the same footing as a homogeneous one. -/
103	theorem isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
104	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
105	    (h : ChartsCoverLocally C f) :
106	    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f) where

109	    refine iSup_le fun i => ?_

112	    refine ⟨(Sigma.ι (fun j => yoneda.obj (X j)) i).app (op T') t, ?_⟩

8	/-!
9	# `IsChartLocusFibre` implies the UNRESTRICTED certificate — the guard, instantiated
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean` reduces `IsChartUniv` to `IsChartLocusFibre` (`:152`) and
12	describes that residue as "`ChartFibrePresented` with its `W` field already discharged — it is
13	`chartLocus`" (`:138`).  `Picard/Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean` separately proves the
14	guard `isEmpty_forall_chartFibrePresented_of_not_injective` (`:219`): no family of
15	`ChartFibrePresented` data exists for a chart map that fails to be injective on some test.
16	
17	**The tree holds the reduction and its own guard as separate facts and draws the consequence
18	nowhere.**  This file draws it.
19	
20	**AN ATTRIBUTION CORRECTION, from a fresh-context audit (2026-07-29, inbox `I-0895`).**  An
21	earlier draft of this header said the instantiation "is what nobody had written".  That
22	overstates it: the term proving the unrestricted certificate below is character-for-character
23	the inner argument that `isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre` was *already* passing to
24	`isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart` (`Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean:177-178`, present before
25	this file).  The unrestricted certificate was never missing — it was sitting inside the
26	existing reduction, unnamed.  What is new here is only that it is *stated*, so that its
27	conflict with the three headers is visible to a reader and to a grep.  The value is routing,
28	not mathematics.
29	
30	The two facts are one instantiation apart:
31	
32	* `IsChartLocusFibre` quantifies `Nonempty (ChartFibrePresented C (abelSigmaChart …) g)` — the
33	  datum for the **unrestricted** Abel chart, with `W` a *free field* of the structure.  Neither
34	  `chartLocus` nor the restriction open `V` occurs in its statement, nor in the proof of
35	  `isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre`.  So the `:138` docstring is wrong: the `W` field is not
36	  "already discharged — it is `chartLocus`"; it is universally quantified inside a `Nonempty`,
37	  and the criterion consumes it for the unrestricted `f`;
38	* therefore `IsChartLocusFibre` **implies** `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (abelSigmaChart …)` at
39	  `V = ⊤`, hence `Mono`, hence injectivity on every test.
40	
41	That conclusion is exactly what three headers cite as the *reason* the unrestricted route
42	fails — the Abel map has the linear systems `|D|` as fibres, so it is not a monomorphism
43	(`Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:54`, `Pic0ChartPair.lean:14`,
44	`Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean:214`).  If those headers are correct then
45	`IsChartLocusFibre` is **unsatisfiable**, and a lane proving its `exists_factor` field is
46	working a false goal.  Note the conditional: the headers are *prose*, so this file establishes
47	an implication, not a refutation.  Nothing in the tree connected the two, and a `sorry`-census
48	cannot flag the connection, because both ends are sorry-free and axiom-clean.
49	
50	## What this file does and does not settle
51	
52	It does **not** prove the Abel chart is non-injective — that is asserted by prose in three
53	places and proved nowhere.  This file makes the conditional precise and machine-checked, so
54	that the question becomes a single fork rather than a docstring:
55	
56	**AND THE THREE HEADERS' STATED REASON IS NOT AVAILABLE AT THE DEGREE THIS ATLAS USES**
57	(`ajcr-p3`, 2026-07-29, inbox `I-0903`; `Picard/Pic0ChartAbelNonInjective.lean`).  They blame
58	the linear systems `|D|`, i.e. `h⁰ ≥ 2`.  But at `deg D = g` with `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(D))` the
59	rank anchor forces `h⁰ = deg + χ = g + (1 - g) = 1` **exactly**
60	(`h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one`, `RiemannRoch/FLVClass.lean:412` — verified at
61	that line, not taken on report), and
62	`n = g` is what `chartTwist` targets.  So the fibre is a single point precisely where the atlas
63	reads it, and a non-injectivity witness must instead exhibit a divisor-scheme point where `H¹`
64	*fails* to vanish — the fork is about the **carve**, not about `|D|`.  A generic-degree `|D|`
65	argument is exactly the wrong instrument here, and an earlier draft of this header (and my own
66	messages to two lanes) used it; retracted.  Read `I-0903` before pricing the fork:
67	
68	* if the Abel chart is non-injective on even one test, `IsChartLocusFibre` is FALSE
69	  (`not_isChartLocusFibre_of_not_injective`);
70	* if `IsChartLocusFibre` holds, the Abel chart is a monomorphism and the three headers are
71	  wrong (`mono_abelSigmaChart_of_isChartLocusFibre`).
72	
73	Those two are contrapositives of one implication, so this file does **not** decide between
74	them — neither branch is proved here, and a lane must settle the fork before spending a session
75	on `exists_factor`.  The fork is `AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-c.c9-chartlocus.abel-noninj`.  The
76	honest repair — a fibre criterion at the *restricted* chart, whose `exists_factor` quantifies
77	only over points landing in `V` — is a different statement, is not weakened by anything here,
78	and is landed separately in `Picard/Pic0ChartRestrictedFibre.lean`.
79	
80	## Main declarations
81	
82	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_abelSigmaChart_of_isChartLocusFibre` — the
83	  reduction's residue implies the UNRESTRICTED certificate.  One term; `V` never appears.
84	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mono_abelSigmaChart_of_isChartLocusFibre` /
85	  `AlgebraicGeometry.injective_abelSigmaChart_of_isChartLocusFibre` — the consequences the
86	  three headers deny.
87	* `AlgebraicGeometry.not_isChartLocusFibre_of_not_injective` — **the guard, instantiated at
88	  the Abel chart**: non-injectivity on one test refutes `IsChartLocusFibre` outright.
89	-/

109	variable (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
110	  = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
111	
112	/-- **The reduction's residue implies the UNRESTRICTED certificate.**
113	
114	`IsChartLocusFibre` supplies a `ChartFibrePresented` datum for *every* test and *every* class,
115	for the unrestricted `abelSigmaChart`; the criterion consumes exactly that.  So the restriction
116	open `V` — the thing `IsChartUniv` is parameterised by and the thing the atlas is built from —
117	plays no part, and this is one term.
118	
119	This is the statement `Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean:138` implicitly denies when it calls the `W`
120	field "already discharged — it is `chartLocus`".  `W` is a free field of the structure;
121	`chartLocus` is not mentioned anywhere in `IsChartLocusFibre`. -/
122	theorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_abelSigmaChart_of_isChartLocusFibre
123	    (h : IsChartLocusFibre C π n rep m Z hdeg) :
124	    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg) :=
125	  isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented _ fun T g => (h T g).some
126	
127	/-- **Hence the Abel chart is a monomorphism** — which `Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:54`,
128	`Pic0ChartPair.lean:14` and `Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean:214` all assert it is not,
129	the linear systems `|D|` being its fibres. -/
130	theorem mono_abelSigmaChart_of_isChartLocusFibre
131	    (h : IsChartLocusFibre C π n rep m Z hdeg) :
132	    Mono (abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg) :=
133	  mono_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf
134	    (isOpenImmersion_presheaf_abelSigmaChart_of_isChartLocusFibre rep m Z hdeg h)
135	
136	/-- **Hence the Abel chart is injective on the points of every test**, unrestricted.
137	
138	The elementwise form, which is where the contradiction with `|D|` would be exhibited: two
139	distinct effective divisors in one linear system give one class, and this says that cannot
140	happen over any test whatsoever. -/
141	theorem injective_abelSigmaChart_of_isChartLocusFibre
142	    (h : IsChartLocusFibre C π n rep m Z hdeg) (T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ) :
143	    Function.Injective ((abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg).app T) :=
144	  injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf
145	    (isOpenImmersion_presheaf_abelSigmaChart_of_isChartLocusFibre rep m Z hdeg h) T
146	
147	/-- **THE GUARD, INSTANTIATED AT THE ABEL CHART**: if the Abel chart fails to be injective on
148	even one test, `IsChartLocusFibre` is false.
149	
150	`isEmpty_forall_chartFibrePresented_of_not_injective`
151	(`Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean:219`) is the general statement; it lives in the same
152	file as the criterion and was never instantiated at the Abel chart, which is the only chart the
153	tree has.  This is that instantiation, and it is the declaration a lane should consult before
154	attacking `exists_factor`.
155	
156	So the fork is sharp: EITHER the three headers are right that the Abel map is not a
157	monomorphism — and then `IsChartLocusFibre` is unsatisfiable and `isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre`,
158	though sorry-free, can never fire — OR they are wrong. The two cannot both hold. -/
159	theorem not_isChartLocusFibre_of_not_injective (T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ)
160	    (hT : ¬ Function.Injective ((abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg).app T)) :
161	    ¬ IsChartLocusFibre C π n rep m Z hdeg := fun h =>
162	  hT (injective_abelSigmaChart_of_isChartLocusFibre rep m Z hdeg h T)
163	
164	end
165	
166	end AlgebraicGeometry

theorem divFamEps_eq_of_le_of_quotientData (F : DivFam C R π g)
    (x₁ : Grassmannian.grFunctorAff k
      (↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (windowM_choice π hπ g • fiberWeilDivisor π) ⊤)) g R)
    (x₂ : Grassmannian.grFunctorAff k
      (↥(Scheme.divisorSections k
        ((windowM_choice π hπ g + windowS_choice π hπ g) • fiberWeilDivisor π) ⊤)) g R)
    (hproj₁ : Module.Projective R
      ((R ⊗[k] ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k
          (windowM_choice π hπ g • fiberWeilDivisor π) ⊤)) ⧸
        F.window (relThetaPairH1_windowM C π hπ g)))
    (hrank₁ : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,
      Module.rankAtStalk
        ((R ⊗[k] ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k
            (windowM_choice π hπ g • fiberWeilDivisor π) ⊤)) ⧸
          F.window (relThetaPairH1_windowM C π hπ g)) p = g)
    (hproj₂ : Module.Projective R
      ((R ⊗[k] ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k
          ((windowM_choice π hπ g + windowS_choice π hπ g) • fiberWeilDivisor π) ⊤)) ⧸
        F.window (relThetaPairH1_windowMS C π hπ g)))
    (hrank₂ : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,
      Module.rankAtStalk
        ((R ⊗[k] ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k
            ((windowM_choice π hπ g + windowS_choice π hπ g) • fiberWeilDivisor π) ⊤)) ⧸
          F.window (relThetaPairH1_windowMS C π hπ g)) p = g)
    (hle₁ : x₁.toSubmodule ≤ F.window (relThetaPairH1_windowM C π hπ g))
    (hle₂ : x₂.toSubmodule ≤ F.window (relThetaPairH1_windowMS C π hπ g)) :
    divFamEps hπ g F = (x₁.toSubmodule, x₂.toSubmodule) :=
  -- `divFamEps` is the pair of the two `DivFam.window`s BY DEFINITION (`divFamEps`,
  -- `Picard/DivisorFamilyWindow.lean`), so no `Quotient.ind` is needed: the two components
  -- are the two hypotheses' subjects on the nose.  Descending to a representative instead
  -- makes the window unfold through the section-ring algebra tower and blows the recursion
  -- limit -- measured, at exactly the two `Prod.ext` legs.
  Prod.ext
    (divisorWindowQuot_eq_of_le_of_quotientData F _ x₁ hproj₁ hrank₁ hle₁)
    (divisorWindowQuot_eq_of_le_of_quotientData F _ x₂ hproj₂ hrank₂ hle₂)

/-- **THE ε-PAIR IDENTITY FROM CONTAINMENT ALONE — the satisfiability probe, discharged.**

The module docstring says this file owes a satisfiability check: the window-quotient hypotheses
are *determined* by `F` rather than consumer-chosen, so the live failure mode is not vacuity but
**unsatisfiability** — a reduction to a false hypothesis passes every `sorry` census and axiom
probe, because it is then a theorem.

**The check comes back positive, and better than positive: the hypotheses are already landed,
unconditionally, on `DivFam`.**  `Picard/DivSchemeFrameCover.lean` carries
`DivFam.projective_window_quotient` and `DivFam.rankAtStalk_window_quotient` for *every*
`F : DivFam C R π g` at *every* window `a ≥ windowM_choice`, discharged inside from the
representative's own certificate — which `DivFam` has by construction, since
`CertifiedDivisorFamily` is a triple carrying one.

So at the two pinned ledger windows the ε-pair identity needs **only the two containments**:

* `hle₁` is DDR-3's `le_vanishingSubmodule` at the seed;
* `hle₂` is the named DDR-5 second-window boundary.

**What this does and does not settle.**  It settles that the ε-half of U2 is not a reduction to
a false hypothesis — the hypothesis holds for every `DivFam`, so it is satisfiable wherever a
`DivFam` exists.  It does **not** produce a `DivFam` over the chart ring: that is the class
half, and it remains the whole open obligation (protection `I-0492`'s widening is the route).

**The sharp reading, and it is a demotion of this file's own headline.**  If the window-quotient
facts were already unconditional on `DivFam`, then the ε-half of U2 was never gated on a
certificate *at all* — not even on the weakened `HasCertifiedAdaptation` of
`Picard/DivRepChartClassUnivAny.lean`.  What the earlier sessions read as "U2 needs a
certificate" was the **class** requirement leaking into the ε statement through the carrier:
you cannot *write* `divFamEps hπ g F` without an `F`, and every `F` carries a certificate.  The
ε layer never asked for one beyond that. -/
theorem divFamEps_eq_of_le (F : DivFam C R π g)
    (hπ' : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
    (hO : Sheaf.h0 (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1)
    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
    (x₁ : Grassmannian.grFunctorAff k
      (↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (windowM_choice π hπ g • fiberWeilDivisor π) ⊤)) g R)
    (x₂ : Grassmannian.grFunctorAff k
      (↥(Scheme.divisorSections k
        ((windowM_choice π hπ g + windowS_choice π hπ g) • fiberWeilDivisor π) ⊤)) g R)
    (hle₁ : x₁.toSubmodule ≤ F.window (relThetaPairH1_windowM C π hπ g))
    (hle₂ : x₂.toSubmodule ≤ F.window (relThetaPairH1_windowMS C π hπ g)) :
    divFamEps hπ g F = (x₁.toSubmodule, x₂.toSubmodule) :=
  divFamEps_eq_of_le_of_quotientData hπ F x₁ x₂
    (DivFam.projective_window_quotient hπ' g hO hχ (windowM_choice π hπ g)
      (relThetaPairH1_windowM C π hπ g) le_rfl F)
    (DivFam.rankAtStalk_window_quotient hπ' g hO hχ (windowM_choice π hπ g)
      (relThetaPairH1_windowM C π hπ g) le_rfl F)
    (DivFam.projective_window_quotient hπ' g hO hχ
      (windowM_choice π hπ g + windowS_choice π hπ g)
      (relThetaPairH1_windowMS C π hπ g) (Nat.le_add_right _ _) F)
    (DivFam.rankAtStalk_window_quotient hπ' g hO hχ
      (windowM_choice π hπ g + windowS_choice π hπ g)

/-- **U2's ε-identity and its `DivFamZar` class from the WEAKEST certificate obligation.**

Inputs: `g ≠ 0` (which discharges the scalar, `Picard/DivRepChartClassUnivFree.lean`) and
`HasCertifiedAdaptation` at the high-window universal seed — *some* adaptation certified,
not the extraction's.  Output: a locally certified class over the chart ring whose `ε` is
the universal tautological pair, i.e. exactly what U2 asks a producer to exhibit.

The two are packaged together on purpose: a class without its ε-value does not serve
`isChartClause_iff_forall_classify_eq` (`Picard/DivRepChartRange.lean`), and an ε-value
without the class cannot be fed to it.

**WARNING, and read it before planning off this theorem** (inbox `I-0705`, confirmed by the
no-go's owner): the hypothesis `HasCertifiedAdaptation` is **refuted** by
`forall_not_isCertified_of_straddling` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyAffStrict.lean:127`) whenever the
seed's local equations are connected and meet both pinned fibres — that theorem concludes
`∀ A n, ¬ A.IsCertified n`, which is this existential's negation at the same binder.  Whether
the high-window universal seed straddles in that sense is **unmeasured**, and the same no-go
refutes the older `(D.divisorAdaptation hD).IsCertified g` spelling too, since that is one
instance of its `∀`.  So this theorem is a sound *reduction* whose hypothesis may be false;
do not read it as "U2 is one certificate away". -/
theorem exists_divFamZar_divFamEps_eq_universal_pair_of_hasCertifiedAdaptation
    (hg : g ≠ 0)
    (hca : (univSeed C hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j hO hchi
        (windowBound_pos_of_ne_zero C hpi g hO hchi hg)).HasCertifiedAdaptation
      g (isGenerator_univSeed C hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j hO hchi
        (windowBound_pos_of_ne_zero C hpi g hO hchi hg))) :
    ∃ G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C RZ pi g,
      divFamEps hpi g (DivFam.mk G)
        = ((divUniversalFstWindow C pi hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j).toSubmodule,
           (divUniversalSndWindow C pi hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j).toSubmodule) := by
  obtain ⟨A, hc⟩ := hca
  -- The witness is named explicitly rather than left to `refine ⟨_, ?_⟩`: with the
  -- adaptation coming from the existential, the placeholder is not determined by the
  -- goal and the elaborator leaves it open (measured -- the kernel reported an unsolved
  -- goal at exactly this shape).
  exact ⟨_, ThetaGeneratorSeed.divFamEps_certifiedFamilyOfAdaptation hpi
    (divUniversalFstWindow C pi hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j)
    (divUniversalSndWindow C pi hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j)
    (univSeed C hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j hO hchi
      (windowBound_pos_of_ne_zero C hpi g hO hchi hg))
    (isGenerator_univSeed C hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j hO hchi
      (windowBound_pos_of_ne_zero C hpi g hO hchi hg))
    A hc hO hchi
    (divUniversalSndWindow_le_highWindow_divisorWindow C hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j hO hchi
      (windowBound_pos_of_ne_zero C hpi g hO hchi hg))⟩

certificate is a local one through the trivial one-member cover, so no Zariski shrinking is
involved. -/

/-! ## The chart-typed side: no adaptation, in no degree

separation statement needs.  `not_isCertified_of_isPreconnected_of_witnesses` is stated about
one adaptation `A` and one degree `n`; the widening claim is about *all* of them, and that
strengthening is free because the hypotheses mention neither. -/

/-- **The chart-typed carrier cannot see a straddling connected divisor — for any adaptation,
in any degree.**

`hx₀`/`hy₁` are the witnesses that the support genuinely meets both pinned vertical fibres:
a point outside `V₀` and a point outside `V₁`.  Note that no leak hypothesis appears — clause

rather than about a failed proof attempt. -/
theorem forall_not_isCertified_of_straddling
    {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
    (hconn : _root_.IsPreconnected d.supportLocus)
    {x y : relCurve C R} (hx : x ∈ d.supportLocus) (hy : y ∈ d.supportLocus)
    (hx₀ : x ∉ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover pi)).V₀ : Set (relCurve C R)))
    (hy₁ : y ∉ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover pi)).V₁ : Set (relCurve C R))) :
    ∀ (A : DivisorAdaptation C R pi d) (n : ℕ), ¬ A.IsCertified n :=
  fun A _ => A.not_isCertified_of_isPreconnected_of_witnesses hconn hx hy hx₀ hy₁
